rows.variant_name_as_reported: rs2305619 and/or rs3816527 (homozygosity for the minor allele)
rows.verbatim_source: Other, N=145, F=13, CI=0.10, ref. / Homozygous, N=67, F=13, CI=0.21, P=0.04
rows.note: Composite exposure: homozygous for minor allele of rs2305619 and/or rs3816527; same result as the rs3816527 composite row. Units are chemotherapy courses, not patients. 'Other' group (N=145, F=13) pools heterozygotes and non-carriers, so separate counts left null; control counts not printed. Alleles given only as 'minor allele'. Log-rank test; 6-month cumulative incidence 21% vs 10%.

rows.variant_name_as_reported: rs2305619 and/or rs3816527 (homozygosity for the minor allele)
rows.comparison_as_reported: homozygosity for the minor allele vs other
rows.verbatim_source: homozygosity for the minor allele of PTX3 rs2305619 and/or rs3816527 was an independent predictor of invasive mold infections (hazard ratio=5.06, 95% confidence interval 1.68-15.2; P=0.004), after adjustment for the type of underlying disease.
rows.note: Paper says 'hazard ratio' from Stata stcrreg competing-risk model (Fine-Gray), hence subdistribution HR. Adjusted for type of underlying disease. Composite exposure; duplicate of rs3816527 composite row.

paper_note: Haematologica 2018 letter: 212 intensive chemotherapy courses (185 acute leukemia patients), 26 invasive mold infections; main text reports only a composite PTX3 exposure (homozygous minor allele of rs2305619 and/or rs3816527), with log-rank results overall and by pre-existing neutropenia plus one adjusted competing-risk HR; single-SNP results are in unavailable supplementary figures; alleles not named.
